name: W Boston
positioning: A Theatre District hotel whose rooms riff on Boston's rebels, from Aerosmith to Edgar Allan Poe, steps from the city's theaters and Boston Common
best_for: Theatergoers who want to be seconds from Boston Opera House and Wang Theatre
Travelers who like playful, design-led rooms with a local story

facts.text: Guests can cross Boylston Street to explore Boston Common, the nation's oldest city park.
Room headboards are a playful distortion of early Colonial Boston's classic wood paneling.
Rooms have a cupboard stocked with local spirits.
The signature W bed has a featherbed mattress, floating frame and coffered headboard.
Penthouse II Suites offer views of downtown Boston from the corners of the highest floors.
W Lounge has a fireplace, creative small plates and rotating DJs on Thursday, Friday and Saturday nights.
The Whatever/Whenever service aims to give guests whatever they want, whenever they want it.
The building meets LEED Gold standards.

highlights.text: The hotel's design is inspired by notorious Boston icons, from Aerosmith to Edgar Allan Poe to the Salem witches.
The hotel is in Boston's Theatre District, seconds from performances at Boston Opera House and Wang Theatre.
Handmade wool area rugs in the rooms are inspired by Steven Tyler's jumpsuits.
The Urban Suite, themed on Edgar Allan Poe, is on the 15th floor and has hardwood floors throughout.

considerations.text: Rooms at W Boston do not have a fridge.
The minimum age to check in is 21.
WhataHotel notes the downtown setting has limited parking options.
